title: On Grünbaum's problem for symmetric configurations
summary: Let $g_n$ be the largest number of Euclidean balls of diameter $1$ which may be needed to cover a set of diameter $1$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We study this problem for finite sets invariant under all coordinate permutations. We prove that the exponential growth rate in this symmetric problem can be characterized exactly as a finite-alphabet squared-error rate-distortion supremum $α_0$. Specialized to the two-point case, i.e., for subsets of Boolean cubes, this gives the explicit lower bound \[g_n\ge (1.160235457\ldots-o(1))^n,\] improving the previous best bound $(2/\sqrt3-o(1))^n$.
